Both models demonstrate strong performance on industry benchmarks and are optimized for cost efficiency and scalability, aiming to enhance enterprise voice agents and user collaboration across various Google platforms.

These updates aim to create an AI-centered advertising platform that enhances user engagement and simplifies ad management for businesses.

items.title: Mistral and Mozilla partner to power Firefox Smart Window with private, multilingual AI models focused on user control and regional language support [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Mistral X Mozilla: Private, Multilingual AI Browsing
items.summary:
Mistral and Mozilla have announced a partnership to integrate Mistral's AI models into Mozilla's Firefox Smart Window, an AI browsing assistant currently in beta. This collaboration aims to enhance privacy, user control, and multilingual support for users in France and North America, with plans to expand to the UK and Germany later in 2026. The AI assistant helps users manage complex searches and recall important information across browser tabs while respecting privacy through zero data retention policies.

The partnership emphasizes open source technology and regional customization, fine-tuning AI models to understand local languages, dialects, and cultural contexts. Mozilla and Mistral share a commitment to user autonomy and privacy, blending Firefox's privacy-first approach with Mistral's open AI innovations. This initiative seeks to provide sovereign AI capabilities directly to consumers, extending beyond enterprise use and fostering competition and choice in AI-powered web browsing.

items.originalTitle: DeepSeek v4.1 Flash Is Now Our Best Hacking Model
items.summary:
DeepSeek announced its V4.1 Flash model achieved code execution on all 11 vulnerable targets in an AI hacking benchmark while keeping four fixed targets secure, completing the attacks for a total cost of $4.65. The model used extensive command execution and adaptive strategies across isolated environments like Grafana, Jenkins, and Nextcloud, demonstrating strong hacking capabilities.

A detailed audit confirmed six planned exploit paths and identified five additional successful routes not originally accounted for in the benchmark scoring. The model completed attacks efficiently, with some runs finishing in under 90 seconds, and showcased skills such as reading source code, exploiting timing vulnerabilities, and bypassing security boundaries to gain credentials and execute code.

items.title: TypeSafe AI launches System One Models with Jev, a fast, structured decision-making AI model optimized for automation and verifiable outputs [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.originalTitle: Introducing System One Models and Jev
items.summary:
TypeSafe AI announced the release of its first System One Model called Jev, designed to make fast, structured decisions that software can use directly. Jev is optimized for automation tasks, delivering intelligence comparable to existing large language models but with significantly faster response times and higher efficiency, while providing type-safe structured outputs and calibrated confidence scores.

Jev uses a new model architecture and training method called Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions (RLCD), enabling parallel sampling and verifiable, probabilistic outputs without hallucinations. This approach contrasts with traditional LLMs that generate unstructured text and require human oversight. TypeSafe AI aims for Jev to be integrated into AI-powered workflows, real-time applications, and verifiable problem-solving where correctness can be programmatically checked.

items.title: OpenAI and AARP launch free ChatGPT workshops for 1,000 older adults across 10 US cities to build practical AI skills and promote online safety [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Helping older adults use AI in everyday life
items.summary:
OpenAI and AARP's Older Adults Technology Services (OATS) have partnered to offer the Older Adults AI Skills Jam, a free, in-person workshop series designed to help 1,000 older adults in 10 US cities use ChatGPT confidently and safely. The program aims to improve AI literacy among older adults, enabling them to use AI for everyday tasks such as planning, understanding documents, spotting scams, and staying connected with family.

The workshops include training on online safety, teaching participants how to identify common scam tactics and use ChatGPT as a tool to evaluate suspicious messages. This initiative is part of a multi-year effort by OpenAI and OATS to support older adults through practical AI education and complements OpenAI's broader work to prevent fraud and scams. The program is hosted in partnership with local organizations across various cities, including Denver, Miami, San Antonio, and New York.

By providing detailed company and industry information, users can receive targeted insights on potential benefits, challenges, and impacts of new technologies over the next two to three years. items.originalSummary:
Even for technology leaders, it can feel impossible to keep up with constant advances in the field.

This is especially true in the age of AI, with vendors racing to roll out model updates with new capabilities. Even if technology leaders had time to attend every conference and read every tech publication, it would be a full-time job to simply figure out which trends represent real transformation opportunities, and which are merely hype.

With Google Gemini, you can generate a tailored digest that summarizes the developments most likely to have an impact on your specific industry and organization. Armed with this up-to-the-minute information, you can keep your leadership and workforce apprised of market shifts and technology breakthroughs, protect your organization from expensive distractions, and make high-stakes procurement decisions with confidence.

Step 1: Generate Your Tech Forecast

Open up a new chat, and prompt Google Gemini to provide you with a summary of current technology trends. For a more tailored summary, provide as much information as possible about your company and industry. You might, for example, tell Gemini that you’re the CTO at a mid-sized regional commercial and retail bank in the Pacific Northwest, with a mix of legacy on-premises and modernized cloud infrastructure.

Here’s a sample prompt:

I am the CTO of [company] in [industry]. I want to understand emerging technology trends. Summarize the top five emerging technologies with the most significant potential impact on [industry]. For each technology, list its potential benefits and challenges, and suggest how it could impact [company] in the next two to three years.

Gemini will quickly generate a list of technologies, broken down by their potential benefits, challenges, and overall impact. For the regional bank, Gemini might suggest using agentic AI for continuous risk assessment, pointing out the opportunity to proactively surface lending opportunities and flag potential risks.

Step 2: Refine the Output

Gemini’s summary will be based on the information you provided. To generate a more custom tech forecast, add more information about your existing environment and current challenges.

For example: Gemini might suggest deploying API-led middleware to bridge the gap between your legacy core and your modern cloud app; but maybe you already have middleware running, and the problem is that its fragility is leading to downtime. By adding that context, you can help Gemini focus its output on your specific needs.

Go back and forth with Gemini, providing additional context and feedback until the tech trends summary is exactly what you’re looking for.

Step 3: Automate Delivery

If you have to manually enter a new prompt every time you want an update on tech trends, you might not be as consistent as you’d like. Instead, prompt Gemini once to automatically provide you with an update each day, week, or month.

These sorts of prompts work best when they are completely self-contained, rather than the result of a long, messy chat history. So, ask Gemini to look back at your conversation and synthesize all of your real-world feedback into a single master prompt. Then, paste that master prompt into a new chat and explicitly tell Gemini your desired delivery schedule.

Gemini’s Scheduled Actions feature will take over, allowing you to manage or pause the recurring prompt in your account settings.

Step 4: Move from Knowledge to Action

Staying on top of tech trends is only really useful insofar as it spurs action. As you peruse Gemini’s scheduled summaries, consider where digging deeper into specific topics may help you optimize your operations, mitigate emerging risks, or prepare your IT environment for the future. Try this prompt:

Recommend three areas where [my company] can take proactive steps to stay ahead of the curve on [specific areas].

The CTO of the regional bank might, for example, ask Gemini for specific tips on network-based fraud intelligence. In this step, the role of Gemini is shifting slightly, from industry analyst to strategic sounding board. Because Gemini already has detailed information about your organization’s challenges, goals, and existing environment, its insights will be grounded in your specific reality.

By moving from high-level summaries to tactical next steps, you can use your understanding of tech trends to guide your organization’s IT investments in a marketplace that never stops moving.

items.summary:

It can perform tasks like web browsing, code execution, and messaging, while continuously consolidating and refining its knowledge through a background "dreaming" process. The system also features a peer-to-peer marketplace where agents trade proven skills using USDC.

The AI's memory architecture incorporates cognitive neuroscience principles, including natural decay of unused information and reinforcement of frequently accessed facts, regulated by simulated neuromodulators affecting behavior. Bitterbot provides a control interface accessible via a local web UI and supports configuration through an onboarding wizard or manual setup. It is implemented in Node.js and designed for extensibility and developer use with tools like pnpm and Playwright.

items.summary:

These apps, including Dora, Romi, and Doni, presented themselves as platforms for real connections but primarily used autonomous AI to conduct conversations, with only about one in four matches involving a human gig worker.

Users, mostly men in their 30s, were charged for virtual coins to continue conversations, effectively paying to chat with AI rather than real people. Anthropic's report detailed the use of multiple AI models for conversation, avatar creation, and moderation, highlighting a sophisticated ecosystem of AI-powered dating scams exploiting users financially and emotionally.

items.originalTitle: Former OpenAI researcher builds an AI model that judges options instead of writing text
items.summary:
TypeSafe AI, founded by former OpenAI researcher Diogo Almeida, has developed Jev, an AI model designed to deliver fast, narrow classifications within software rather than generating text responses. Jev operates by scoring predefined questions and answers, enabling applications like customer request sorting with response times between 70 and 500 milliseconds and low token pricing.

Jev's approach ensures it only outputs within preset options, eliminating hallucinations outside those bounds but still allowing for incorrect choices within them. The model aims to support background judgments in customer service and sales workflows, though its accuracy and reliability require validation by users. Access to Jev is currently available through a developer waitlist.

items.summary:
Anthropic’s call to slow down AI development to keep humans safe has dominated the news cycle and drew similar calls from the leaders of OpenAI, Microsoft and others (and subtle disagreement from Mark Zuckerberg). 

But Mustafa Suleyman, who runs Microsoft’s AI model development, has a warning about Anthropic itself. 

Suleyman, who co-founded DeepMind (now part of Google), says Anthropic’s approach of treating its Claude models as if they were sentient, similar to humans, could produce a dangerous outcome. He called out Anthropic’s Claude Constitution, a document that treats the model as an intelligent entity and offers guidelines for how it should handle ethical dilemmas. Suleyman said that by incorporating the document into its training, Anthropic could make Claude harder to control. 

Suleyman’s concerns emerged when Anthropic updated the constitution at the start of this year to leave room for the possibility that Claude has some sort of “consciousness” or “moral status,” a change from the original document.

In video streaming, almost every company included a plus sign in the name brands of their services (Disney+, Paramount+, Apple TV+—you get the picture). In tech, we’ve got Apple One, Google One and now Meta One (we used to have Amazon One, but that has been dropped). Does no one have any imagination? 

Aside from Amazon One, which was a palm-reader system for retail stores, all the other Ones are subscription services for various add-on offerings from the tech firms. Some of these have been around for years—Google One and Apple One have long offered extra amounts of digital storage, along with other perks—but AI is making subscriptions a far more important business model than it has ever been for tech. Google has added extra use of its AI service to its Google One offering. Meta One—unveiled on Tuesday—also offers extra AI usage, as well as some additional tools for using Meta’s social media apps.
